## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

### Modwerk (formerly Octamod)

2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set, 24 since 2026-11-14; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10). 2026-11-14 (second pass): the Digitakt II moved from research to preview: the site builds core 1.0 with library modules in the browser, downloads stay off, OS 1.17 only; the first DT2 library module is Track Names; DT2 phrase modules can continue phrases across empty steps, follow microtimed trigs and save settings in a project archive. Octatrack: a two-step base update for units whose RAM stage is too small; the CPU guard counts the picked machine's price and judges a stopped unit by its last playing load (I105); POLY8 0.3.3 and FM Synth 0.1.3 cost far less while installed on no track (FM Synth 0.1.3 also fixes track 1's LFO 3); `device:price` measures a module's cost; a new Octatrack Diagnostics page on the site. 2026-11-14 (changelog, verification): an Octatrack module set may hold 24 modules (was 20, still temporary); the base may grow to 1.5 MiB, so units on a base older than 2026-11-13 take it as two USB updates, and a base update retries up to four times when a reply goes missing before the write starts. New project and bank events (load, save, reload, new project, Part save and clear) let a module keep its own file beside the project. Amiga 0.3.0 (experimental) adds a SYNC stretch mode that follows the project tempo; in a RAM trial on an MKII an earlier build of it restarted after about 90 s on a twin that also carried a base change under test (I109). Filter Hz 1.2.1 (Rytm MKII, from rytm2_mods' port of 0008-filter-hz) widens the box behind a locked FRQ so kHz values fit; a maintainer ran it on a Rytm MKII on OS 1.74 on 2026-11-14. 2026-11-16 (changelog 2026-11-14/15, LINK.md, TEST_RUNNER.md): Rytm MKII development bases carry a SysEx USB link (screen, memory, keys, encoders, remote flash, and a boot from RAM with no flash write), and a test runner plays scripted cases on rytm-emu or a unit over it. Filter Hz 1.3.0 shows the FX track's delay and reverb HPF, LPF and reverb FRQ in Hz. 2026-11-17 (changelog 2026-11-16/17, verification, module docs): Octatrack base versions start at 0.7 (shown as MODWERK BASE 0.7 on the unit; 0.7.1 to 0.7.5 the same day): PROJ > MODWERK > MODULES switches installed modules on and off; a project remembers which machine each track uses, so a missing machine is named instead of playing FLEX; one module may use 288 KiB (was 128) and may borrow sample memory while installed; windowed modules such as Tuner can come over USB (base 0.7.5); packages are no longer refused for sharing byte runs with stock; every Octatrack module must name its CPU price (`resources.cpuPrice`); `module:doctor` reports DSP register writes against each hook site's contract; stall records name each DSP core's last packet. New Octatrack modules Kits and MIDI Scenes 0.3.0 (experimental ports of octabam's modules, short RAM trials on the owner's MKII); the Octakit draft is removed. New Digitakt I module CC Remap. Rytm MKII: a third base variant, voices; Ping Pong Loop folded into Improved SMPL 0.6.x; size-only updates of several modules run on the author's unit; Analog Rytm MKI builds are refused when the update exceeds the upgrade buffer or touches the boot-flash writers. Goal pages for contributors on the Digitakt II and the Syntakt (no Syntakt module yet). Field diagnostics 12-16 Nov: 87 units. A dialog on the site says the project's future is uncertain and asks for maintainers.

### octabam

Modular Octatrack OS 1.40C "remixer": bus and track effects, FM synth machine, 255 kits, USB audio/MIDI, stock bug fixes. Base of Modwerk. Licence: MIT; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument; README, CHANGELOG and contributing docs read 2026-11-10. 2026-11-03: new midi-follow module (docs/site/usage/midi-follow.md, a test remix); not read further. 2026-11-10: WAVE (wavecf) is a 4-voice wavetable machine on the ColdFire, reduced from CHOMPI WAVE, heard on an MKII in builds W1-W6 (I58); XF CURVE offers 13 crossfader curves, run on a contributor's MKII on 2026-11-06; KEYBUS publishes each track's block peak for side-chain keys (make check only); a demand-loader soak with STEM REC froze an MKII (I57, open). 2026-11-12/13: new FRAME GUARD module holds a late frame interrupt out of a window in which the DSP's frame exchange stalls at START or a program change (I82); with it 32 first STARTs and 192 program changes ran clean on an MKII with a 20-channel USB capture. MIDI SCENES: CLEAR, COPY and PASTE SCENE act on the MIDI and audio locks together in either track mode, and a scene held across the MIDI key shows its locks as a fresh press does. 2026-11-15 (FAILURE_MODES, TRAPS, CHIP, MODULES): a program change to a demand effect that was not loaded stopped the audio in about two runs of three on an MKII while panel and USB still answered (I108); moving the loader's copy from the head to the end of DSP core B's frame cured it in 12 of 12 runs. A new gate lets a DSP instruction form ship only with a stock site, a register row or a module proven on a unit; a tool lists modules changed since their unit proof. 2026-11-16 (unreleased, 2026-11-14/16): REMOTE, an event ring a host reads over USB with PEEK and four commands; SCOPE and TUNER share the TEMPO key in the octabam remix; DRUMMER's KIT BALANCE takes step and scene locks; a LIM stereo peak limiter after MIX on RESONATOR and SHATTER; MIDI SCENES sends the Part's value when no scene locks a CC; SCALES keeps one audio scale per bank and Part; a ColdFire instruction-form check reports forms but refuses none yet. 2026-11-17 (CONTRIBUTING, remixes, TESTING): contributors' own remixes now live in remixes/community/<name>/ and may not use the octabam name; cxosc-core moved there. One module per pull request. CI runs one unit per gate job and skips units whose gates already passed for the same image.

### OT Kyoti FW

Feature and fix builds keeping the stock feel: mute modes, pattern jump, sidechain compressor, varispeed, repitch. Tested on an MKI. Licence: MIT; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument. 2026-11-02: MUTE_MODES KEYHOLD fixes octabam#934: with SIDECHAIN_COMPRESSOR a muted track that had been the KEY played again once KEY moved away; held tracks now keep the post-FX cut until unmuted. Confirmed on an Octatrack MKI. 2026-11-09: RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT reloads one track's slice of the Part from the card ([BANK] + [TRACK n]) or a whole pattern ([PTN] + [BANK] + trig), landing on the next step while playing; a click from a copy with interrupts masked was fixed on the unit (I60); the REC_TRIG_MUTE fix was confirmed on hardware. 2026-11-10: octabam's HOOKS chain lets RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT and FREE LOOP share their UI-tick site in one image (emulator-checked, not flashed). 2026-11-13 (NOTES.md): BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 is being rebuilt as one packaged DSP engine for the Modwerk base (not flashed); its host check is bit-exact against the emulator twin. 2026-11-14 (README, NOTES, module README): RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT takes over the landing rules of the author's Clyps work: a reloaded track lands one tick before the step boundary, so it is never a step late; a FULL reload's sound settings change only with the first trig that sounds, never on a ringing sample; trig conditions (1:2, PRE, FILL, also after STOP and PLAY) carry on as if the saved sequence had always played. A twelfth hook at the stock trig-condition reset does this. The standalone image passed every walk-through item on the author's MKI the same day; not yet run in an octabam-built image. 2026-11-17 (README, NOTES, FLASHING, Clyps manual and scope): new CLYPS, a clip launcher after Ableton's Session view: [PTN] + [BANK] shows the active track's sequence in all 16 patterns of a bank; a trig loads one onto the track (with its sound when [FUNC] is held) while the others play on; originals, per-track temp saves and card reloads put things back. It keeps ~10 MB of sample memory and always ships with DIRECT JUMP, never beside RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT. KYOTI V1.8 (RELOAD + DIRECT JUMP) and V1.8C (CLYPS) replace V1.7; every image now carries the three bug fixes. DIRECT JUMP V7.2.2 releases tracks that SILENCE TRACKS mutes just before a jump, curing a pop on the unit (an earlier fix inferred in the emulator did not); V7.3 counts a jump's position and trig conditions from the last normal pattern change, confirmed by ear in V1.8C on 2026-11-16.

### STEP VIEW (Octatrack step editor)

A step editor and piano-roll pitch view for the eight MIDI tracks (MIXER + MIDI): all tracks at 32 steps a row, one track's 64 steps, notes with VEL and LEN per step. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-08. 2026-11-11: the Split view also shows the audio tracks (each step's trig and its p-locks), and Pages with the audio tracks shows the cursor track's page values beside that page's SETUP. 2026-11-12 (README): works on both sides, the 8 audio tracks and the 8 MIDI tracks (MIDI switches); YES opens a lock window with every p-lock on a step (Pitch stays MIDI only). Later on 2026-11-12: each row of the Tracks view shows only that track's own steps, with its length at the row's end (briefly a separate lengths view). 2026-11-13 (README): every row follows its own track while playing; Pages shows the cursor step's parameters underneath in the lock window's five columns; a note window for MIDI steps; FX SETUP locks through a patch to octabam's PLOCKS P2; the newest parts (lock-window layout, FX SETUP locks) are emulator-only so far. 2026-11-14 (README): the Split view became STEPS in the arranger's ARR menu, so MIXER + MIDI cycles Tracks, Pages and Pitch; track lengths are set at each row's end (SCALE PER TRACK); copy, clear and paste work in full on the audio tracks; SETUP pages show in the lock window (locked only for FX with PLOCKS P2). v0.9/v0.9.1 (2026-11-14): MIXER + MIDI toggles Tracks and Pages only; Pitch opens with a double press of a MIDI track key; the MIDI track-names feature was dropped; undo and redo up to nine steps. 2026-11-15 (README): the track number flashes M for muted MIDI tracks too; a track's length flashes when picked, and YES opens the Octatrack's SCALE window for that track. 2026-11-16 (README): the STEPS view is now called Arranger Steps; no change in function.

### AERIA OS

An operating system of its own for the Octatrack MKII, not a patch of Elektron's OS: a weather-driven multi-effect on inputs A-D (up to seven effects whose knobs the chosen weather moves) and an 8-track sequencer groovebox (sampler, sub, FM, noise, Karplus-Strong and polyphonic MIDI machines, p-locks, ratchets, per-track cellular automata), plus LFOs, a Lorenz attractor and boids as modulators. ColdFire part in C, effects in hand-written DSP56300 assembly. Installing it removes the stock OS until it is reinstalled from the card; both keep their saved data in the same battery-backed SRAM, so back up before switching. The build uses the Modwerk SDK's tools (not included); aeria-os/HARDWARE.md and AUDIO.md map the MKII for writing an OS from scratch, largely from octabam's and Modwerk's documents. Some effect folders (head, tap) are marked as someone else's work. Made with Claude Code (README). Found by GitHub search 2026-11-13. 2026-11-14: docs/CHANGELOG.md lists every release build and what was checked on the unit; docs/LOG.md is the request log of the 9-13 Nov build, with the hardware findings now on the Octatrack page and incidents I83-I86.

### telos (elekloader OS)

An elekloader build that is flashed once and then links more mods at every boot from a store on the unit, so new mods need no new firmware: .elemod files go over USB (SysEx with the non-commercial id 0x7D, each file read back and checked by CRC-32), and a MODS (TELOS) page at the end of SETTINGS switches them on or off for the next boot. A boot that crashes within 10 s of linking makes the next boot link nothing (one safe boot). Only +Drive-style mods (code and .bss, no patch sites). On the Digitone mk1 the store is 2 MB of raw +Drive sectors outside every area stock uses, so it never shows in Transfer; up to 63 files. Planned for the other devices elekloader supports. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-17: the Octatrack port is in the repo (octatrack/, 0.4, emulator only): .elemod files on the CF card in /ELEKLOADER/MODS (copied by USB DISK MODE or a card reader) are linked at the card's first mount, before the project load; unlike the Digitone's, these mods may patch the OS (sites), checked against stock bytes, written with interrupts masked when no task is stopped inside a site, and refused when the OS already ran them before the mount (code 23). 14 of the shop's 15 non-USB octabam conversions link together (about 61 KB); USB mods stay flash-only. DSP code from the card goes through elekloader's dspload-ot. On both devices each saved project now keeps the list of mods that ran, and loading one whose mods differ offers to switch them (LOAD PROJECT MODS?). A poc branch adds site-writing and memory-region mods for the Digitone (POC.md).

_Related: builds on `elekloader` (README: part of elekloader; built as an elekloader mod with core-dn1 and its +Drive boot linker) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_
